reviewDescription: I bought this dress to tie dye. The fabric needs to be a natural fiber, so 100% cotton is ideal, but rayon is also a natural fiber. And, I thought this would dye really well. I was so excited to get it and put dye on it. I washed it and treated it with soda ash before adding the dye and ice. The next day, after my ice had melted, I checked to see if I needed to add more dye or ice and I noticed that the spot that had the most ice was still white. Not a big deal, but I thought it was weird since that's never happened before. And, I started wondering if my fabric was actually polyester or nylon or something not natural. The procion dyes I use will only bond to natural fibers. So, I added more dye, soda ash, and ice. We were expecting rain overnight. And, I had a sweatshirt that I wanted to dye as well. I threw dye and soda ash on it and placed both of my buckets outside for the night so that the rain would activate the dye/soda ash. I have done this numerous times and it has always worked because I've made sure to purchase cotton or rayon clothing for this purpose. So you can imagine how upset I was the next day to discover that everywhere the rain pelted the fabric of this dress was WHITE. The dye didn't take because it was clearly NOT rayon like it says in the item description. Please make sure the clothing is labeled correctly. After I rinsed my dress and washed it, I was left with a dingy, spotty, 99% white dress that I cannot wear because I can't dye it, and now it looks dirty. So it's trash. The 90% cotton sweatshirt, however, dyed beautifully. DON'T buy this dress to dye. You'll waste your time, money, and dyes.
